description:
Operator: name the beneficiary, its website and its Lightning address.

`restricted`, so the runtime requires the caller to be the operator, proven.

It was a constant in the source, which made changing who the money goes to a
deployment. A charity can be replaced, renamed, or rotate its wallet, and
none of that should need anybody to touch code.

Changing this never rewrites history: every settlement records the
beneficiary it actually paid at the time, so a player can always check where
the money went rather than where it goes now.

dpop_token.description: Proof that the caller holds npub. Either the grant envelope that receive_npub_proof returned, or the raw JSON of a kind-27235 Nostr event signed by npub: content "", a `u` tag holding this tool's exact name from tools/list, created_at within 60 s of now, and a random `nonce` tag.

lightning_address.description: Where the charity share is actually sent, e.g. name@wallet.com

name.description: The beneficiary's name, as players should see it.

npub.description: The patron's Nostr public key (npub1...). Tool fees are paid from this patron's balance; dpop_token proves the caller holds it.

website.description: Where a player can check them out.

name: beesknees_set_charity
title: Set the charity
